name: Database Server: Installation and Maintenance
summary: Installing, configuring and keeping a database server alive — the work that begins where writing queries ends.
prerequisites: Both are required: the language and the terminal. No programming language needed beyond SQL.
syllabus: Installation, initial configuration and the parameters that actually matter
Memory, storage layout and the filesystem underneath
Roles, grants and least privilege inside the database itself
Routine maintenance: statistics, vacuum, bloat and reindexing
Upgrades and version migration without losing a weekend
PostgreSQL in depth, with MySQL, SQL Server and Oracle alongside

PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and Oracle: one job, four vocabularies

Connections: the maximum, and why raising it is rarely the fix

GRANT and REVOKE over schemas, tables, columns and rows
Default privileges: the permission that appears with the next table
Autovacuum: what it does, when it falls behind and how to notice
Table and index bloat: measuring it before fixing it
ANALYZE, statistics and a planner deciding on stale numbers
Reindexing, concurrent rebuilds and the lock each one takes
